problem: "f ∘ g ... exists only when C ⊆ A" states a sufficient condition as if it were necessary. f ∘ g is defined whenever every output of g lies in A, that is, when image(g) ⊆ A; if g is not surjective this can happen even though C is not contained in A.
fix: Write: f ∘ g is defined whenever image(g) ⊆ A; a simple sufficient condition to state is C ⊆ A.

problem: The closing clause "since two elements of B with the same image do not affect g ∘ f" is wrong as written: if both those elements lie in the image of f, they do break injectivity of g ∘ f. The point only holds for elements of B outside the image of f.
fix: Say: g need only be injective on the image of f; two elements of B outside that image may share an image under g without affecting whether g ∘ f is injective.

problem: "Composition also carries quality along" is vague wording; a student will not know what "quality" means here.
fix: Say: composition preserves injectivity and surjectivity — if f and g are injective then g ∘ f is injective, and similarly for surjective.
